title: Death Metal History and Vocabulary
description: Listening literacy: lineage, the thrash transition, Florida and Stockholm as production doctrines, then the branches. Scenes, not celebrity lists.

sourceReferences.title: MIT Heavy Metal 101
sourceReferences.notes: History, listening, culture, songwriting tropes, harsh vocals — not celebrity lists. Extreme metal is a sound and a construction problem.

modules.title: Before it was named
learningObjectives: Place death metal in thrash, hardcore, and tape-trading soil
Listen for riff, kit, and vocal as equal parts

modules.title: Two founding scenes
learningObjectives: Contrast Florida and Stockholm as two production doctrines
Treat the mix as part of the composition

modules.title: Branches
learningObjectives: Name a branch by construction, not by compliment or insult
Keep brutal, technical, progressive, dissonant, and melodic as different contracts

concepts.name: Pre-death-metal lineage
concepts.summary: Hardcore, thrash, and extreme metal as the soil, not a name-drop.
objectives: Place death metal in hardcore, thrash, and extreme-metal soil without a name-drop list
Name what changed when weight took the job speed had been doing

concepts.name: How to listen to a death-metal record
concepts.summary: Riff, kit, vocal as equal parts. The mix is an argument.
objectives: Listen for riff, kit, and vocal as equal parts
Treat the mix as an argument you can describe, not as fog

concepts.name: The thrash/extreme transition
concepts.summary: When speed stopped being the point and weight took over.
objectives: Mark the transition where speed stopped being the point
Contrast a thrash d-beat section with a death-metal blast as grammars

concepts.name: Harsh vocals as a lineage
concepts.summary: A technique with a history, not a personality.
objectives: Treat harsh vocals as a technique with a history
Describe a vocal as rhythm and register, not as a personality

concepts.name: Scenes, not celebrity lists
concepts.summary: A city, a studio, a tape network.
objectives: Describe a scene as a city, a studio, and a tape network
Refuse a celebrity list as a substitute for that description

concepts.name: How the style spread
concepts.summary: Tapes, zines, and the fact that scenes were postal.
objectives: Explain how the style spread through tapes and zines
Predict why two cities could finish the same move without a single capital

concepts.name: Florida and Stockholm
concepts.summary: Two scenes, two production doctrines, one genre name.
objectives: Contrast Florida and Stockholm as two production doctrines under one genre name
Hear Morrisound versus Sunlight as engineering decisions, not fashion

concepts.name: The Florida sound
concepts.summary: Clarity, palm-mute punctuation, a particular drum sound.
objectives: Name clarity, palm-mute punctuation, and a particular drum sound as the Florida doctrine
Point at those facts on a record instead of naming a roster

concepts.name: The Stockholm sound
concepts.summary: Buzzsaw guitars and a drier, dirtier midrange.
objectives: Name buzzsaw guitars and a dirtier midrange as the Stockholm doctrine
Describe the HM-2 wall as spectrum, not as a brand sticker

concepts.name: Production as a stylistic fact
concepts.summary: The mix is part of the composition.
objectives: Treat the mix as part of the composition
Predict how a drier or wetter guitar changes whether cells fuse or stay separate

concepts.name: Lyrical domains
concepts.summary: Gore, occult, and social disgust as registers — not trivia.
objectives: Treat gore, occult, and social disgust as lyrical registers
Refuse trivia about lyrics as a substitute for musical construction

concepts.name: Double-kick as a historical marker
concepts.summary: When the right foot stopped being enough.
objectives: Mark when the right foot stopped being enough
Hear double-kick as a historical subdivision, not as sport

concepts.name: Brutal death metal
concepts.summary: Lower, thicker, less interested in a sung interval.
objectives: Describe brutal death metal as lower, thicker, less interested in a sung interval
Keep 'brutal' as a construction contract, not a compliment

concepts.name: Technical death metal as a branch
concepts.summary: Density and odd grouping as a scene, not a compliment.
objectives: Describe technical death metal as density and odd grouping as a scene
Refuse 'technical' as a synonym for good

concepts.name: Progressive death metal as a branch
concepts.summary: Longer forms and borrowed jazz/fusion grammar.
objectives: Describe progressive death metal as longer forms and borrowed grammar
Name what the form borrowed without requiring a jazz exam

concepts.name: Dissonant and avant-garde branches
concepts.summary: When the riff stops agreeing with itself.
objectives: Mark the branch where the riff stops agreeing with itself
Distinguish dissonant construction from 'they played wrong notes'

concepts.name: Melodic death metal as a fork
concepts.summary: Harmony that wants to be sung, still under distortion.
objectives: Describe melodic death metal as harmony that wants to be sung, still under distortion
Keep it as a fork, not as a purity test

concepts.name: The grind border
concepts.summary: Duration and blast as a different contract.
objectives: Treat grind's contract as duration and blast, not as failed death metal
Predict why a forty-second song is a different form problem

concepts.name: A second wave of brutality
concepts.summary: What 'brutal' meant a decade later.
objectives: Say what 'brutal' meant a decade later
Contrast early thickness with a later slam or ossuary vocabulary

concepts.name: 1990s technicality
concepts.summary: The first records that treated odd grouping as normal.
objectives: Name the first records that treated odd grouping as normal
Hear 1990s technicality as grammar, not as a later fashion

concepts.name: The later technical/dissonant wave
concepts.summary: 2000s onward: triggers, tighter grids, colder harmony.
objectives: Describe the later technical and dissonant wave as tighter grids and colder harmony
Predict what triggers and edits do to that grammar

concepts.name: Regional dialects after the two capitals
concepts.summary: Quebec, Poland, the American south, and why the accent is the riff.
objectives: Hear a regional dialect in the riff, not in the passport
Compare two later scenes by construction rather than by map trivia
